children: Federal Reserve governor Michael Barr said further rate hikes are likely needed to ensure inflation comes down to target in a timely fashion.

Barr expressed that he supported the Fed's decision to raise interest rates by a quarter-percentage point last week, speaking at an event in Chicago. He noted that risks to achieving the Fed's inflation target have risen.

"Inflation is above our 2 percent target and not clearly trending toward target in a timely way," a published text of his remarks said. "In my base case, further policy adjustments are likely to be needed to ensure inflation comes down to target in a timely fashion."

Barr said the economy has experienced a series of shocks over the past year and a half that has contributed to upward price pressures. Those shocks include tariffs, the conflict in the Middle East, disruptions from Russia's war on Ukraine and more recently, a surge in investment demand to support the artificial intelligence buildout.

At the news conference following September's interest rate decision, Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said the committee's unanimous vote to raise rates shows the central bank's resolve to achieve price stability on a timelier basis.
The probability the central bank will raise interest rates at its October Fed meeting stands around 55%, according to CME's FedWatch tool. That probability was around 9% one month ago.
